subject: Lame duck session of Congress
query: what is a lame duck session
title: What is a lame duck session? Congress returns Nov. 9 after the midterms
answer: A lame duck session is any meeting of Congress held after the November election but before the new Congress takes office on Jan. 3. The outgoing members, not the newly elected ones, still cast the votes. The 2026 lame duck session begins Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, when both the House and Senate return.
body:
The Congressional Research Service defines it simply: a lame duck session "occurs whenever one Congress meets after its successor is elected." The phrase "lame duck" was first used in 18th-century Britain for bankrupt businessmen and by the 1830s was applied to officeholders whose time in office had a known end date. The 20th Amendment, ratified in 1933, moved the start of each new Congress to Jan. 3, so since 1935 any meeting between the November election and Jan. 3 counts as a lame duck session.

According to CRS, there were 25 such sessions from 1935 through 2024, and one has been held in every Congress since 1999-2000. Their main purpose is to finish legislation, most often government funding bills and program authorizations.

For 2026, the House is scheduled to sit for two weeks starting Nov. 9, break for Thanksgiving week and then return until Dec. 17. The Senate sits Nov. 9 and 10, returns Nov. 16 for a week, breaks for Thanksgiving and comes back Nov. 30 for the first three weeks of December. The 120th Congress, elected on Nov. 3, 2026, begins at noon on Jan. 3, 2027.
in_the_news: Congress returns on Nov. 9, 2026, for its first session since the midterm elections, in which Democrats won control of both the House and Senate, according to the AP.

faq.q: Why is it called a lame duck session?
faq.a: "Lame duck" first described bankrupt businessmen in 18th-century Britain and later came to mean officeholders whose term has a known end date.

faq.q: Who votes in a lame duck session?
faq.a: The sitting members of the outgoing Congress, including those who lost or retired. Newly elected members do not vote until they are sworn in on Jan. 3.

faq.q: When does the 2026 lame duck session start?
faq.a: Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, when both chambers return. It runs until the end of the 119th Congress, which ends at noon on Jan. 3, 2027.

faq.q: How often does Congress hold a lame duck session?
faq.a: Every Congress since 1999-2000 has held one. From 1935 to 1998, they happened in only 12 of 32 Congresses.
